recap.text: Crawler Volteeg writes a note in the seventh edition cookbook stating he misses her and does not think surviving is worth it with her gone. Crawler Drakea of the 22nd Edition adds that this is Volteeg's only entry and says fuck everything about this place. At dawn, Carl thinks of that line while Prepotente watches and cannot move.

Volteeg entered the dungeon as a Sturnus bird pet and became a gargoyle, a choice that cost him his ability to sing. Mistress Henspar died on the seventh floor, after which he wrote one entry in a cookbook and spent twenty-six seasons as an NPC guard. Porthus changed his designation to refugee. Volteeg died as a Weeper Commander when he pushed a blitz stick into energy balls to kill Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit.

beats.headline: The seventh edition's only note
beats.text: For the record: the note added by Crawler Volteeg, Seventh Edition, runs to a few lines. He misses her. He misses her so goddamn much. Is it worth it, to survive this place with her gone? No, he does not think it is. Beneath it, Crawler Drakea of the 22nd Edition adds that this is Volteeg's first, last, and only entry in the cookbook, and: fuck everything about this place. At dawn, with Prepotente watching and unable to move, Crawler Carl is thinking of that line.
beats.gist: Volteeg writes in a cookbook that he misses her and surviving without her is not worth it.

beats.headline: Berries under her jacket
beats.text: Before the dungeon, the subject was a bird in a cage, and Mistress Henspar kept it clean. She let him perch on her shoulder at the market. Once he bit a shopkeeper's finger when the man tried to feed him a berry, and she forgave him that night by the fire. After that she hid him inside her jacket and slipped him stolen berries, and he tried very hard not to peep. Back outside, belly full, he would sing for her, and salty tears would run down her cheeks. His birth race is Sturnus. His file says he does not consider himself worthy of love.
beats.gist: Volteeg is a Sturnus and former crawler who wrote a seventh-edition cookbook.

beats.headline: A race that cannot sing
beats.text: The pet biscuit gave the subject speech and a little intelligence. On the third floor he chose to become a gargoyle, and only then did his mind begin to work, and the world stop being simple. A gargoyle cannot sing, not the way he used to. He counts that as a terrible mistake. He remembers standing over her, transformed and screaming, trying to protect her from the scags. Mistress Henspar died on the seventh floor. After that he was not scared any more. There was only the rage. The cookbook came to him then.
beats.gist: Volteeg is a former crawler and cookbook author who became a gargoyle and lost his singing voice.

beats.headline: One entry at the ninth's end
beats.text: He did not notice the hidden words on the seemingly useless prayer cast projection until the very first days of the ninth floor. He spent most of Faction Wars in hiding, like the rest, unable to raise his head for fear of the Conscription spell, reading the words of those who came before him and feeling nothing but shame. He told himself the cookbook had come to him too late. At the very end of the ninth floor, as the orc armies roared in victory, he made his one and only entry.
beats.gist: Volteeg wrote one cookbook entry at the ninth floor's end after hiding during Faction Wars.

beats.headline: Twenty-six seasons without a fight
beats.text: On the tenth floor he took the first deal offered: an unprotected NPC guard in a combat-based external guild for 26 seasons, low chance of survival. He survived without fighting, let alone killing, a single crawler. Nobody wants to fight a gargoyle. On exit, the magic of his adopted race stopped working. In heavy gravity he needs a brace just to stand. He took security work on the Auditor General's compliance barge, among the One-Offs: unique former crawlers with no home. His two friends there are a djinn in a wheelchair and a cave fairy who can no longer fly.
beats.gist: Volteeg is a former crawler and seventh-edition cookbook author.

beats.headline: A pet on the form
beats.text: Now he is on the surface as Weeper Commander Volteeg for the Operatic Collective, racial abilities returned. He was not dragged off to the Bone Clan with the other former-crawler mercenaries: he entered the dungeon as a pet, and someone in the Pacifist Network changed that designation so he reads as a refugee. That was Porthus's doing. Rosetta recognised his strange name and told Porthus, who asked him to his face. He said he was ashamed at his inaction. Porthus told him it is not too late to do something about it.
beats.gist: Volteeg is a former crawler and cookbook author now serving as Weeper Commander for the Operatic Collective.

beats.headline: Show me Mistress Henspar
beats.text: Volteeg, gargoyle, Tank Buttress, top level 71, is dead. The Weepers have a flaw in their fire control. He removed the chamber and filled his tank with dozens of humming energy balls, put Mozart on, and sang along as he turned toward the litter carrying Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit. Told he was too close to the caravan, he answered that this was the point. He lit a blitz stick, said Show me Mistress Henspar, and pushed it into the ball on his lap. Over 10,000 of his fellow soldiers died with him, and the Operatic Collective was eliminated.
beats.gist: Volteeg, a level 71 gargoyle and cookbook author, blew himself up to eliminate the Operatic Collective.
